subject: Renewal: usage fingerprint, churn risk & capacity uplift plan
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: usage fingerprint, churn risk & capacity uplift plan

Hi Priya —

Thanks for taking the time last week. I pulled together a quick usage fingerprint for FluxGrid and a short note on risk drivers we see in the run-up to renewals. Key highlights up front:

- Monthly token spend has grown 38% YoY in the last 12 months but is concentrated in a two-week surge pattern tied to nightly batch inference jobs.
- Median latency for inference calls to the deployed 'redwood-3b-q' model is meeting the SLA, but tail latency spikes during the batch window are impacting downstream timeout retries and increasing cost by ~12%.
- Prefetch/persistent batch opportunities could reduce token cost per inference and shave 20–30% of peak-to-average load.

I attached the raw token report (fluxgrid-q1-token-report.csv) and a short latency sample (latency-sample-snippet.txt). Two asks to keep this moving:
1) Can you confirm whether the nightly jobs are business-critical or if they can be spread or sharded?
2) Would FluxGrid consider a modest committed uplift to cover peak corridor (we've sketched three options in the attached XLSX)?

If it helps, Ben and I can join a 30-minute call next week to walk through numbers and a mutual action plan for the renewal. Proposed times: Tue/Feb 23 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed/Feb 24 14:00–15:00 PT.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Laura —

Thanks for the write-up and the files. Quick answers: the nightly jobs are currently business-critical (they generate the daily feature store used for model scoring). We do have flexibility to spread them over a longer window but that will require some infra dev work (estimating 2–3 sprints).

Michael and I reviewed the spike and the tail latency notes. Two immediate asks for us before any commitment discussion: 1) a short costing exercise that maps the three commit options to projected per-month spend including expected cost savings from batching/prefetch; 2) a simple SLA addendum for peak capacity with clear rollback triggers.

We can take a 30-minute walkthrough. Wed 24 Feb 14:00 PT works for us.

—Priya

Subject: RE: Renewal: usage fingerprint, churn risk & capacity uplift plan

Laura / Karthik —

I reviewed the raw token CSV and modeled three options quickly (high-level):
A) Conservative uplift: +15% commit over current run-rate — lowers unit cost by ~8%, covers burst corridor with modest commit.
B) Corridor commit: +40% commit, includes a small on-demand buffer — lowers unit cost by ~18% and gives 2x burst headroom.
C) Aggressive prepay: +80% commit + prefresh cache layer — lowers unit cost by ~28% but requires contract term extension (12 -> 18 months) to make the economics attractive.

Notes: the latency tail is the immediate ops risk; if we can get engineering to spread the nightly jobs, the effective burst and cost go way down (Ben's back-of-envelope shows ~20% token reduction). For the SLA addendum Priya wants: we can propose a Peak Capacity ride-through clause (30-day notice, automatic throttling to a smaller model if sustained >X% over baseline for Y days) plus one-time credit if we miss the rollback triggers.

I recommend we lead with Option B in the call — it balances spend reduction and runway. If Priya signals risk aversion we offer Option A + a 60-day pilot for prefetch.

Ben
